text:
alex: saw a weird one in staging — a dashboard briefly showed rows from another org during a canary roll.
juniper: ugh, seen that before? any repro steps?
alex: yes. repro by rapidly toggling the canary flag while prefetch is on. sometimes the prefetch response gets cached and served across workspaces.
liam: is this the same prefetch cache key bug where we didn't include the rollout namespace in the key?
alex: looks related. also telemetry shows metrics attributed to the wrong org id for those requests.
ana: (typo: ana) that telemetry misattribution worries me — could mask quota hits.
juniper: can you paste the header dump from the failing trace?
alex: here:
```
GET /internal/console/prefetch
Headers:
  x-org-id: 8241
  x-workspace-id: 8241-UI
  x-rollout-variant: canary-7
  authorization: Bearer token-redacted
Response cached TTL=30s key=console:prefetch:8241-canary-7
```
liam: aha — cache key uses x-org-id but our routing occasionally receives x-workspace-id when proxy rewrites for internal routes. mismatch -> wrong cache reuse.
juniper: so the proxy strips x-org-id in some fast-paths and downstream service sees only x-workspace-id? that's backwards incompatible.
ops: deploy-bot triggered: canary-toggle v0.82 -> v0.83 at 1732123470
ana: steps I propose:
  1) hotfix: compute cache key from canonical org header fallback order: x-org-id || extract-from x-workspace-id (prefix) || user sub from token.
  2) add a strict guard: if both headers present but disagree, fail prefetch and log with rate limit so we can count occurrences.
  3) patch telemetry attribution logic to prefer canonical org id and add metric tag fallback so quotas can't be bypassed.
  4) rollout UX: add visible indicator in console when prefetch was served from cache and which org it was attributed to (for debugging).
alex: agree. small nit: extracting from x-workspace-id will need regex, but ok.
liam: also add unit test: simulate proxy rewrite (strip x-org-id) and ensure we don't leak prefetches across tenants.
juniper: ops, can you block the canary until we ship the hotfix? if it's only in staging still, we can iterate. if prod, rollback.
ops: it's in a partial prod canary at 10% — I'll pause rollout in 5 mins unless we push a hotfix fast.
ana: I'll own telemetry patch, liam can do cache-key hotfix, alex will add the UX indicator follow-up.
liam: will open PR with tests and link here.
alex: thanks. logging note: when we detect disagreeing headers, include request-id + route + short stack for triage. keep logs low-volume.
juniper: also add a quick dashboard: "prefetch-header-disagreements" with sample rows so product/support can see.
ops: paused canary at 1732123498
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for rollout v0.83 -> v0.82 by ops at 1732123502 :white_check_mark:
liam: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/pulls/412 (draft) — implements canonical key + tests.
ana: telemetry PR coming in 30m.
alex: good catch everyone. followups: 1) hotfix merge + deploy, 2) enable aggressive logging for 24h, 3) dashboard + UX task. I'll create tickets.
juniper: thx — let's keep this thread for final verification logs.
